questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. My husband would not be back until late and I decided to settle down in a comfortable chair and read a book.

B. I put the children to bed early and prepared some coffee.

C. It had been a tiring day and I was looking forward to a quiet evening.

D. Soon I was sitting comfortably with a cup of coffee and the book.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'CABD'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some __grammatical or contextual __connections between them. Also, the first sentence of a passage is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. 

__
 
• Sentence C is the independent sentence and introduces what the subject was thinking of doing. It states how the subject had a tiring day and was looking forward to a quiet evening. 
 
• So, sentence C is the first sentence after rearrangement. 
 
• Sentence A describes how the subject knew that her husband would come late and how she decided that she would relax by reading a book. Thus, to maintain continuity, sentence A comes in the second position. Hence, A follows C.__
 
• Sentence B which explains the actions taken by the subject after she decided what to do should come after sentence A, to maintain continuity on the topic. 
 
• Sentence D is the concluding statement of the passage as it provides further information regarding how the subject finally was sitting and reading her book. 

Thus, the correct order after rearrangement is option 3 i.e. CABD.

*So, the correct paragraph is : (**C) It had been a tiring day and I was looking forward to a quiet evening. (A) My husband would not be back until late and I decided to settle down in a comfortable chair and read a book. (B) I put the children to bed early and prepared some coffee. (D) Soon I was sitting comfortably with a cup of coffee and the book.***

• Devoid is an adjective that means entirely lacking or free from.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

He clarified that he wasn’t the one to send the controversial news to the newspaper

options.text: He said, "I am not the one to send the controversial news to the newspaper."
He said, "He hadn’t been the one to send the controversial news to the newspaper."
He said, "I wasn’t the one to send the controversial news to the newspaper."
He said, "He wasn’t the one to send the controversial news to the newspaper."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'He said, "I am not the one to send the controversial news to the newspaper."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **indirect speech **and we need to convert it to **direct speech.**
 
• When we change **an indirect speech to direct speech**, we use the following rules - 
 
 
• The **reporting verb clarified **is changed to **said**. 
 
• The **conjunction that **is replaced with **inverted commas ("...") **to show the direct speech. 
 
• A **comma (,) **is added before the direct speech part. 
 
• The first word of the direct speech is in *capital letter. *
 
• The **verb (wasn't)** is changed to its **present tense form am not.** 
 
• The **pronoun he **is changed from **second person **to **first person I. **
 
 
 
• So, by following the above rules, we get the direct speech as - He said, "I am not the one to send the controversial news to the newspaper."

Thus, **option 1 **is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Rajesh said to Vandana, "You must buy a beautiful dress for your birthday."

options.text: Rajesh told Vandana that she might buy a beautiful dress for my birthday.
Rajesh told Vandana that she must buy a beautiful dress for her birthday.
Rajesh told Vandana that he would buy a beautiful dress for her birthday.
Rajesh told Vandana that you must buy a beautiful dress for your birthday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Rajesh told Vandana that she must buy a beautiful dress for her birthday.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an assertive sentence. 
 
• While changing the narration of an interrogative sentence, we need to follow these steps -
 
 
• 
 The reporting verb said changes to told. ( This is because we use told when we normally say who is spoken to which in this case is me. In other assertive sentences which does not have a direct personal object, the reporting verb said remains unchanged.)
 
 
• 
 The **conjunction 'that'** is used in place of commas and inverted commas. 
 
 
• 
 The **pronouns you** and **your** is in second person and should be changed to third person **she** and **her. **
 
 
• 
 The **verb buy** is in present tense form and remains unchanged. 
 
 
 

​Eventually, we will get the final sentence- Rajesh told Vandana that she must buy a beautiful dress for her birthday.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In general, the **modal must **is changed to **had to **in indirect speech. 
 
• Since the option is not listed, we select the option which leaves it the same.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

Anurag said that he __is being fined__ by a policeman for not wearing a mask last evening.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'had been fined'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part has an error in the tense used. 
 
• The underlined part states *is being fined *which is in the **present tense format. **
 
• But the incident occurred in the past (last evening) and ended there itself. it was not a continuous event. 
 
• Thus, we need to use the **past perfect continuous tense** for the underlined part. 
 
• Hence, the underlined part should be replaced with **had been fined ** which is the past perfect continuous tense form. 
 
• So, **option 2 **is the correct answer. 

***Correct sentence - ****Anurag said that he **had been fined__**** **by a policeman for not wearing a mask last evening.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The work cannot be completed on time ______ you work for longer hours.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'unless'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence has two clauses - 
 
 
• **Main clause - ***The work cannot be completed on time*
 
• **Subordinate clause - ***you work for longer hours. *
 
 
 
• To join the two clauses, we need to use a **subordinating conjunction.**
 
 
• We can thus negate **even **as it can be used as an adjective, a verb or an adverb but not a conjunction. 
 
• **Because** is used to show/give reason. It is followed by a complete sentence with its own subject and verb. - *She usually eats at home, **because **she likes cooking.*
 
• **Since **is used as a conjunction to introduce a reason. -* It’s so long **since **I saw them.*
 
• **Unless **means; except on the condition that. Unless needs a main clause to make a complete sentence. - *She will be sick **unless **she stops eating.*
 
 
 
• From the above, we can conclude that **unless **is the best fit word for the given blank. 

***Correct sentence - ****The work cannot be completed on time **unless **you work for longer hours.*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The ancient banyan tree is worshipped by the villagers.

options.text: The villagers worshipped the ancient banyan tree.
The villagers are worshipping the ancient banyan tree.
The villagers worship the ancient banyan tree.
The villagers have worshipped the ancient banyan tree.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**The villagers worship the ancient banyan tree.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in passive voice. As per the question we have to change it into active voice.
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject (objective case) + to be + past participle + Object (subjective case) (Passive voice)
 
• Subject + infinitive + Object (Active voice)
 
 
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *Fresh vegetables are sold by the grocer. (Passive voice)*
 
• *The grocer sells fresh vegetables. (Active voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject (objective case) of the given sentence is ‘the ancient banyan tree’.
 
• The object (subjective case) of the given sentence is ‘the villagers’.
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• **is worshipped **will be changed to worship.

Correct sentence - The villagers worship the ancient banyan tree.
